what: Valmont makes galvanised steel structures: the poles that carry streetlights, traffic signals, power lines and mobile phone antennas, and the centre-pivot irrigation systems that water American farms.
customers: Utilities, transport departments, telecom operators and farmers in North America and abroad.
money: utility, lighting, transport and telecom structures and coatings
moat: Galvanising plants and pole fabrication close to customers, plus Valley irrigation, one of two brands American farmers buy, sold through established dealers.
risks: Farm equipment demand follows crop prices, which have fallen
Revenue has been flat around $4.1B for three years
Only four analysts cover the stock
opportunities: 15.2 times earnings with an 8.5% net margin
Utility grid spending is rising sharply to serve data centres, and Valmont makes the poles
watch: Infrastructure segment orders, especially from utilities.
